# Independent review: 992

Candidate: d0c85b2b93a6f29e23cdf9c6b7f19963d266b9aa. URL: http://127.0.0.1:18797/leetcode/992/. Run: 992-review-1-c3711b80, 2026-10-26. Reviewer: this independent review session; no named human or model identity asserted. Target: basic Python, lists, loops, functions, elementary recursion. Frozen rubric: specs/leetcode-review-gates.md, weights 15/20/20/20/15/10. Applicable canonical preference: faithful Python, then TypeScript. No publication assessment.

## Cold walkthrough (saved before opening repository source, tests, author notes, or earlier reviews)

Used real Chromium via Playwright, desktop 1280×900. Read only the frozen rubric before opening the URL. English initially selected. Inspected cold-final.png visually as well as rendered text. Cold screenshots: `992-evidence/992-review-1-c3711b80/cold-initial.png` and `cold-final.png`.

| Teaching step / question | Action | Observable result | My causal paraphrase |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 01: what is being counted? | Read definitions and click Inspect next interval six times | [0,0] excluded (1 type), [0,1] included (2), [0,2] included (2), [1,1] excluded (1), [1,2] included (2), [2,2] excluded (1). Running counts 0,1,2,2,3,3. | A nonempty consecutive interval counts once by position if its set of values has size k; repetitions do not create new types. Answer 3. |
| 02: what repeated work can be saved? | Read baseline, wrong-rule example and cancellation example | Baseline extends every l through every r; 200,010,000 extensions at max n. Exactly-one-window rule misses one at r=2; full length includes singleton. At-most counts 6 and 3. | Counting all valid suffix starts in each at-most window avoids restarting a scan. Subtraction cancels fewer-than-k intervals; over-k intervals are absent from both. |
| 03: how do left boundaries encode all starts? | Append three endpoints, inspect window cards, removal log, start badges and ledger each time | r=0 boundaries 0/0, frequencies {1:1}/{1:1}, contributions 1−1=0. r=1 boundaries 0/1, stricter window deletes 1 at index 0, 2−1=1. r=2 boundaries 0/2, limit-2 freq {1:2,2:1}; stricter window deletes 2 at index 1, 3−1=2. Ledger running totals 0,1,3 retains previous rounds. | Earlier invalid starts stay invalid when appending. Shrink until the first valid start; all later starts are valid. Difference between earliest starts isolates exactly-k intervals. Highlight marks endpoint, not changed data. |
| 04: can I predict a new endpoint? | Before reveal predicted 2 at r=3 of [1,2,2,3,1], k=2. Select “2: starts between the boundaries” then reveal. | Correct feedback: left_2=1, left_1=3; [1,3] and [2,3] qualify; singleton does not. | Both 2 occurrences must leave the limit-1 window, but only initial 1 leaves limit-2. Their boundary gap is two. Independently enumerated suffixes confirms this. |
| 05: how is this executable Python? | Read explanation, expand full submission in browser | Helper adds dictionary counts, repeatedly decrements outgoing values, deletes zero keys, advances left, adds right-left+1, then caller subtracts two helper totals. Text discloses sequential scans vs aligned visual frames. | r=1 stricter transition maps to decrement freq[1], delete key, left+=1, total+=1. Each pointer only advances; two passes stay linear with expected constant-time dictionary operations. nums is read only. |

Fresh independently chosen input prediction before source audit: [2,1,2,3], k=2 should return 4: [0,1], [0,2], [1,2], [2,3]. Endpoint contributions 0,1,2,1; final boundaries 2/3. Counterexample to “one exactly-k window adds one”: at r=2, starts 0 and 1 both count, so that rule undercounts. Counterexample to adding full valid-window length: suffix [2,2] has one type. UI exposes seven presets only, no custom input; the fresh input will therefore be a **code check**, not a UI experiment. The quiz is a separate transfer check and explains both wrong choices. No missing causal explanation was supplied by source/author notes during this walk.

Cold-read assessment: tiny hand enumeration precedes sets, at-most abstraction, invariant, then dictionary code. New terms and endpoint units are defined. Before/after boundaries and individual removals are visible. Browser text already explains cancellation, earliest validity, empty limit-0 windows, termination and cost. Actual novice comprehension is not measured.

## Subsequent audit

The following audit was performed after the cold record above was saved.

### Candidate and source receipt

`git rev-parse HEAD` returned the requested d0c85b2b93a6f29e23cdf9c6b7f19963d266b9aa. Only this report and its evidence directory were untracked. No candidate files were edited. Independently fetched served bytes equal checkout bytes for index.html, solution.py, python-code.js, core.js, app.js, copy.js, local style.css and shared common.js/style.css. SHA-256 identities:

Read the rendered-state contract only after saving the cold record. Audited index.html, app.js, core.js, copy.js, solution.py, style.css, shared locale consumer, metadata, registration language table and both test scripts. No earlier 992 review report exists in this checkout other than this report, so there are no earlier required IDs to close. BRIEF was not needed.

### Official problem and canonical language

Read the [official statement](https://leetcode.com/problems/subarrays-with-k-different-integers/) normally through the web tool: asks for a count of contiguous intervals with exactly k distinct integers; examples return 7 and 3; n≤20,000 and 1≤nums[i],k≤n. No access bypass. Saved lesson-local official.json also contains the Python3 callable snippet. Canonical `class Solution` / `subarraysWithKDistinct(self, nums, k) -> int` preserves that callable and integer return; built-in `list[int]` annotations preserve the List[int] input semantics. This is executable Python, not an analogy. No non-Python language contract or supportedLanguages exclusion applies. Read `LANGUAGE_FILES`: Python maps exactly to solution.py, python-code.js, PYTHON_SOURCE.

### Execution and invariants

Inspected tests before executing. Commands from repository root (all returned exit 0):

```
OUTPUT_DIR=specs/reviews/992-evidence/992-review-1-c3711b80 python3 -B leetcode/992/tests/numerical.py
OUTPUT_DIR=specs/reviews/992-evidence/992-review-1-c3711b80 node leetcode/992/tests/browser.cjs
python3 -B scripts/register_leetcode_lesson.py 992 --validate-only
```

Preflight returned no output, success. `lesson-entry.json` complexity is exactly the single nonempty string `O(n) expected time; O(n) auxiliary space`.

The reused scripts retain their “author self-check” JSON labels; these are independent reruns of inspected author tests, not an assertion that those labels establish review independence. numerical.json reports 6,503 small cases, 45,267 frames, max n 20,000, exact source mirror and 95 unique paired translation keys. Its oracle materializes intervals independently, checks mutation, earliest legal starts, both contributions, prefix totals, frequencies and removal indices. Duplicate-key detection occurs before parsing could discard keys. Localization consumer selects index 0/1 of each pair, matching the audited copy representation.

Separately executed the actual solution.py with `runpy.run_path`, comparing 16,739 valid cases (all length 1–5 arrays over 1…n, every valid k) to independently materialized interval sets; all matched and input lists remained unchanged. The fresh code check [2,1,2,3], k=2 returned predicted 4 and oracle 4. Separate core trace check produced boundary pairs (0,0), (0,1), (0,2), (2,3), contributions 0,1,2,1 and cumulative 0,1,3,4. This custom case was never represented as a browser-input experiment.

Boundary execution includes singleton, all equal k=1, all distinct, k=n and too few types. At n=20,000, all equal k=1 gives 200,010,000; all equal k=n gives 0; all distinct k=1 gives 20,000; all distinct k=n gives 1. At limit 0 the helper deletes the appended key and reaches left=r+1, contributing 0. Nonnegative limits ensure shrink terminates before reading beyond the appended endpoint. Keys are present exactly for positive frequencies, so dictionary length is distinct count. Both pointers advance at most n times per scan; two scans give expected O(n) time, worst-case O(n) dictionary space, without mutating nums. Baseline n(n+1)/2, O(n²) expected time and O(n) space are consistent with its actual loops.

### Rendered interaction and bilingual checks

Browser rerun: Chromium 156.0.8078.4, Linux, real headless Chromium with executable path environment honored and Playwright resolved through NODE_PATH. browser.json passed with no lesson runtime errors. Every round of all seven presets was independently compared with interval enumeration in each locale; results: 3,7,3,6,2,1,0. Initial state, endpoints, disabled buttons, hand count, complete rewind and replay and reset passed. Snapshot window text and ledger recover exactly on undo/replay. The fixed hand experiment is independent of simulation presets.

Independently re-read the dense official-1 final state at 390 px in both locales: limit-2 boundary 0→3 with 3 distinct before shrinking; removals leave frequencies 1,1,0, deleting only on 0; final {2:1,3:1}. Limit-1 boundary 3→4 removes 2 to zero, final {3:1}. Starts 0,1,2 are over k, start 3 exactly k, start 4 fewer; contributions 2−1=1 and total 7 agree with ledger 0,1,3,6,7. Formula in both locales renders all operands `(r−left_k+1) − (r−left_(k−1)+1) = left_(k−1)−left_k`. Chinese removal, exclusion and cancellation explanations match the mathematical meanings, not merely the existence of their keys.

Prediction reveal is initially disabled. All three choices give appropriate correct/incorrect feedback; changing choice hides old feedback until reveal. The question is always the fixed exercise input, so preserving its answer when the separate simulation preset changes is correct. Locale switches preserve selected preset, endpoint, prediction/reveal and expanded source. Narrow zh→en→zh retains correct localized H1 and document title with #992 and the exact official URL.

Copy success equals canonical text; four fallback transfers (two per locale) each first write and read back a distinct sentinel, then force automatic-write denial, check focus/full source selection and invoke Linux Control+C. Clipboard readback equals canonical source including final newline each time. Decoded offline mirror, window.PYTHON_SOURCE, displayed code via textContent, copied text and downloaded bytes all match actual solution.py without trimming. Offline file:// source and interaction work; storage denial does not break locale or simulation.

Keyboard Enter activates reset, locale and related links; Tab moves focus and a visible 3px outline remains. The narrow table scrolls with ArrowRight while retaining column associations. Related links were followed: #76/#step2 actually explains expansion/shrinking with coverage counts; #2916/#step1 actually groups subarrays by right endpoint and sums squared distinct counts. Labels accurately describe those local served continuations in both languages; this does not claim deployment acceptance for the other lessons. The only recorded sibling warning is #2916’s missing root favicon.ico, not a broken #992 resource or teaching target.

### Layout, contrast, screenshots

Generated screenshots only in this run’s directory; earlier evidence untouched. Visually inspected cold-final.png, en-320-stage.png, zh-320-stage.png, zh-390-stage.png, en-1440-stage.png, both zoom200-stage.png files and en-320-right.png. Dense windows, before/after counts and removal logs remain readable, with no observed text collision. Narrow cards stack. At 320 px the English “current r” wraps but remains associated with the highlighted value; data, indices and endpoint marker remain distinct. The table is intentionally wider than its region, explains keyboard scrolling, and right-scrolled capture exposes exactly-k and cumulative columns. No page overflow at 320/390/736/1440. All measured buttons/selects reach 48px minimum height. Closed selected labels pass measured font budgets with 32px arrow reserve; the screenshot confirms the selected Official 1 label is complete.

200% was tested with CSS root zoom=2 in Chromium, not browser-chrome zoom or a physical device. Screenshots show the complete dense state and retained column meanings. Focused stage captures hide sticky navigation only during capture, as documented by the test; page screenshots/navigation geometry retain it. Cold full-page screenshot has a sticky-nav capture overlay, which is not a reproducible settled content collision.

Reviewed contrast helper uses correct sRGB coefficients .2126/.7152/.0722 and tests black/white/primaries plus #747474 on black = 4.492948… below 4.5. Actual solid-color ratios: body 16.087, hint 7.744, disabled control 7.079, normal control 13.397, current value 8.171, exact badge 9.809, table headings 7.079, focus vs panel 9.809. Disabled controls remain readable and distinguishable. Scope is the sampled solid-color states, not arbitrary gradients or assistive-technology certification.

Required open IDs: **none**. No implementation correction requested; no prior finding closure claimed.

Weighted score: **100/100**. Scores mean independently clear under the frozen rubric; they do not assert perfect pedagogy or measured human understanding. Acceptance thresholds satisfied: ≥85, every dimension ≥3, complete applicable evidence, zero required open findings.

Conclusion: **accepted** for candidate d0c85b2b93a6f29e23cdf9c6b7f19963d266b9aa in this review scope. # Independent review of lesson 995

Candidate: `d84cfb5265103d6d321fdc3f0d5dd4b3e17ac13c`.

## Cold browser walkthrough

Real Chromium via Playwright, 1280×900, English initial locale. Screenshots: `995-evidence/995-review-1-c18c137a/cold-initial.png` (full page, inspected), `cold-scan.png` (completed scan). Only the rubric and browser-rendered lesson were read before this record.

| Teaching step / question | Action | Visible result | My causal paraphrase |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1: What does a flip do, and why flip an original 1? | Read definitions, click Show next flip twice, then Previous hand step. | Original 010 becomes 100, then 111; rewind restores 100. Index 1 changes 1→0→1. Answer 2 flips. Domain and zero-based indices are stated. | A window toggles every included bit, including ones. Overlap can restore a bit. Counting original zeros alone cannot decide moves. |
| 2: Why must the leftmost unresolved zero force a start? | Read forced-choice explanation, counterexample, cancellation argument; expand baseline Python. | Later starts cannot reach i; duplicate starts cancel; 010 refutes zero-count/k and only-flip-zeros. Baseline copies then writes each of k cells. | With earlier starts fixed, start i is the only unused start that can change i. A 1 forbids that start. Every feasible solution must share these choices; overflow means impossible. Repeated k writes are the optimization target. |
| 3: How do boundary events replace writes? | Read parity/XOR definitions; check all three positions of preset A, then rewind once. | At i=0 ledger 0→0→1, test 0^0, flip expires 2; effective 100. At i=1 ledger 1→1→0, test 1^1, flip expires 3; effective 111, last cell still Pending. At i=2 ledger 0→1→1, test 0^1, skip; final 2. Rewind restores exactly two ledger rows, no final result. | Earlier covering flips determine the current bit by odd/even count. Expire before testing because the old window excludes its endpoint. After each decision, checked prefix is all ones. Actual cell values and checked-status are separate. |
| 4: Does expiry change a new answer? | For displayed 0110,k=2 choose “3 flips” before clicking Reveal & explain. | Correct prediction; 0110→1010→1100→1111, starts 0,1,2. Explanation says start 0 expires at i=2 and original 1 becomes effective 0. | Overlap parity before expiry is insufficient: removing the expired window forces the third flip. This is a transfer exercise rather than the initial 010 replay. |
| 5: How does this become Python and what does it cost? | Expand submission details; read mapping and boundary discussion. | `Solution.minKBitFlips`, expire length n+1, expiry XOR before test, overflow guard, start XOR and endpoint record; no assignment to nums. O(n) time/O(n) space explicitly excludes visual snapshots. | Each of n iterations does constant work instead of k cell writes; initialization is linear. End n is legal but not scanned. k=1 counts zeros; k=n mixed bits cannot succeed. |

The visual scan's i=2 transition maps to `parity ^= expire[i]` (0^1=1), then `(nums[i] ^ parity)==0` is false, so no flip. This mapping was reconstructed from displayed Python, before source audit.

Independent predictions recorded before source/execution: `[0,0,1,0,0],k=2` → 2 (00100→11100→11111, starts 0,3). Counterexample `[0,1],k=2` → −1 (01→10, no legal remaining window); a zero-count shortcut would suggest one operation. The browser offers only presets A–H, so these are pending **code checks**, not custom-input UI experiments.

## Independent computation and invariants

Executed the actual canonical file via Python `importlib.util.spec_from_file_location`, with `python3 -B`. My separate oracle enumerated every subset of legal window starts, explicitly toggled its cells and minimized the number of starts producing all ones. This differs from the author's BFS and from the greedy/expiry implementation. Exhaustive n=1..8, every binary array and every valid k: **3,586 cases matched**, and input lists remained equal to their before copies.

Fresh predictions above were confirmed against both actual Python and this oracle: 00100,k=2 → 2; 01,k=2 → −1. These were code checks, not UI custom-input runs. Further independent boundaries: [1],1→0; [0],1→1; [0,0],2→1; [1,0],2→−1; [1,1],2→0. For the fresh success, legal starts 0 and 3 produce 11100 then 11111. For the counterexample, the only legal start changes 01 to 10; there is no way to fix the suffix. This excludes the tempting rule that fixing the first original zero is sufficient or that each zero can always be handled independently.

Manually checked the dense official preset B beyond the initial hand case:

| i | entry / expiry toggle / parity before test | original XOR before | action / after parity |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 0 | 0 / 0 / 0 | 0^0=0 | start 0, expires 3 / 1 |
| 1 | 1 / 0 / 1 | 0^1=1 | skip / 1 |
| 2 | 1 / 0 / 1 | 0^1=1 | skip / 1 |
| 3 | 1 / 1 / 0 | 1^0=1 | skip / 0 |
| 4 | 0 / 0 / 0 | 0^0=0 | start 4, expires 7 / 1 |
| 5 | 1 / 0 / 1 | 1^1=0 | start 5, expires 8 / 0 |
| 6 | 0 / 0 / 0 | 1^0=1 | skip / 0 |
| 7 | 0 / 1 / 1 | 0^1=1 | skip / 1 |

Rendered i=5 agrees: 6/8 checked, starts 0,4,5, three flips, no final result. Effective cells are already all ones, but indices 6 and 7 remain pending. At completion the answer is 3. All advertised preset answers were independently covered by the subset oracle: A–H = 2,3,−1,2,1,0,−1,1, and matched browser descriptions and terminals in both locales.

The invariant is about the instant **after expiry, before testing**: the earlier prefix is fixed at 1 and parity counts earlier windows still covering i modulo two. Selecting i never changes that prefix; skipping is safe only for an effective 1. Failure preserves the earlier prefix but leaves the current 0 pending. Browser preset C shows this: final −1, flips so far 0, index 2 current/pending, not fixed. Finite scanning ends after n tests or the first impossible required window. Cancellation permits each start to be considered once; uniquely forced starts yield minimum count, not merely a feasible count.

Actual Python allocates n+1 expiry cells, scans n positions, and performs constant work per iteration. It does not reconstruct snapshots or mutate nums. Time and auxiliary space are O(n), including initialization, even for immediate failure or all ones. The displayed baseline copies n elements and can toggle k cells at each of O(n) starts: O(nk) time/O(n) extra space; k≥1 prevents a lost scan term at a zero parameter. Legal endpoint n is stored and not scanned; the strict `i+k>n` rejection is correct.
